class.name: SnapHelper
class.brief_description: Aligns the list to a snapped item after fling or scroll stop.
class.description:
SnapHelper is the port of [i]RecyclerView.SnapHelper[/i]. Attached to a RecyclerView, it takes over flings and, when the list stops scrolling, snaps it so the target item aligns to the viewport. Use the built-in [b]LinearSnapHelper[/b] (center-align to the item nearest the viewport middle) or [b]PagerSnapHelper[/b] (align a full page per fling):
[codeblock] var snap := LinearSnapHelper.new() snap.attach_to_recycler_view(recycler_view) [/codeblock]
[b]Note:[/b] the three Android snap hooks ([code]findSnapView[/code], etc.) are C++ virtuals, not script-overridable. To customize snapping you would need a C++ subclass.

method.name: attach_to_recycler_view
method.description: Binds the helper to a RecyclerView (sets [method RecyclerView.set_snap_helper] and registers a scroll listener) and immediately snaps the current content.

method.name: detach
method.description: Unbinds the helper and removes its scroll listener.

method.name: on_fling
method.description: Called by the RecyclerView before an inertial fling starts. Returns true when this helper took over (it already smooth-scrolled to the snapped target).
